thesis_statement: Williams owns irreplaceable natural-gas infrastructure at the center of the AI-power demand corridor: Adjusted EBITDA +6% with the midpoint raised $200M on the Momentum Midstream acquisition connecting Haynesville supply to Gulf Coast LNG and power demand, a Blackstone JV adding $5.34B of low-cost capital, and take-or-pay contracts making growth increasingly fee-like - though earnings retain commodity-cyclic sensitivity through gathering volumes.

base.summary: Transco expansions (Leidy Access, Garden Connector, Power Express upsized) and Momentum contribution deliver mid-single-digit EBITDA growth on the raised ~$8.4B midpoint with dividend coverage above 2x.
drivers: Socrates phase one complete; phase two on track for 4Q 2026

bull.summary: AI data-center power demand keeps landing on Transco's corridor (Power Express upsizing), LNG expansion (Momentum, Gulf Coast) lifts Haynesville throughput, and the fee-based mix pushes the multiple toward premium infrastructure.
drivers: Blackstone Power Innovation JV with $5.34B low-cost capital
Power Express upsized on data-center demand

bear.summary: Natural-g Prices stay depressed, drilling and gathering volumes fall, growth-project returns compress, and the elevated leverage against a heavy capex program limits flexibility.
drivers: large multi-project capex concurrent execution risk

key_risks: Commodity-linked volumes: despite take-or-pay growth projects, the legacy gathering business rides producer drilling economics.
Concurrent-execution risk: Momentum integration, Socrates phase two, Transco expansions, and the Blackstone JV all executing simultaneously.
Net debt ~$30.6B with a ~26.9x forward earnings multiple that prices the growth already.
Regulatory (FERC) timing on Transco expansions is a recurring variable.
